target.name: Zipline
target.founder: Keller Rinaudo Cliffton, Keenan Wyrobek, Will Hetzler

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $8.6B.

data.narrative:
Zipline, a Series H autonomous delivery platform, is valued at $7.6B following $1.63B in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of four same-sector comparables spanning drones and autonomous systems, including both private and public entities at similar valuation tiers: Wayve ($8.6B, Series D), Joby Aviation ($6.9B, public), Nuro ($6.0B, Series G), and Archer Aviation ($3.3B, public).

Peer-median analysis anchors the valuation work, yielding $6.4B across the four-company set. This method remains the sole directly applicable triangulation approach given limited public market comparables in the autonomous systems space and the private nature of most peers. The peer distribution spans $3.3B to $8.6B, establishing a bracketing range around the median.

The triangulated valuation range centers on $6.4B (median), with a low bound of $5.5B and high bound of $7.4B. Zipline's current $7.6B valuation sits modestly above this range, suggesting a modest premium to peer medians—approximately 3.4% above the high bound. Key uncertainties include the durability of venture-stage valuations in autonomous systems given prolonged pre-revenue or early-revenue profiles, and the representativeness of public comparables (Joby, Archer) whose market valuations may not reflect private growth-stage economics. Limited methodological depth—single-method triangulation—warrants cautious application.
